sections.h2: Who do I call about a Madison County, KY tax bill?
sections.html:
Call the Sheriff's Office about the bill itself and the PVA about the number it is based on. Madison County keeps a third office, the County Clerk, for deeds and for bills that have gone delinquent.

  • The Sheriff's Office sits at 135 W Irvine, Suite B01, in Richmond (859-623-1511). It posts a secure online portal for searching and paying bills, takes payments in person or by mail, and tells owners never to mail cash.
  • The Property Valuation Administrator handles assessed value and exemptions. The sheriff's tax page gives its number as 859-623-5410.
  • The Clerk's Richmond Branch, 321 N. Madison Ave., records deeds. A second branch at 304 Chestnut Street in Berea does vehicle and marriage license work.

Under KRS 134.119 the sheriff may also take payment from someone paying on the owner's behalf, which helps when an heir or an agent is clearing a bill before a sale.

sections.h2: What kind of county is Madison County for a seller?
sections.html:
Madison County is a college county that has been adding residents for decades. Eastern Kentucky University is in Richmond, Berea College is in Berea, and the two cities are the only incorporated places in the county. Census counts show the effect: 28,541 people in 1940, 53,352 in 1980, 82,916 in 2010 and 92,701 in 2020, with the July 2025 estimate at 101,696.

The county was set up in December 1785 and is named for James Madison. Daniel Boone and a party of settlers began Fort Boonesborough on the Kentucky River in 1775, and it is now a state historic site. Interstate 75, U.S. 25, U.S. 421 and KY 52 cross the county, which borders Fayette County to the north and Jessamine, Garrard, Rockcastle, Jackson, Estill and Clark counties around the rest of its edge.

Housing differs from the rural counties around it. Of 36,148 households at the 2020 census, 40.5 percent of occupied units were rented, and 8.1 percent of all units sat vacant. About 36 percent of residents lived in rural areas, so many sellers hold parcels in places such as Kingston, Waco or Speedwell rather than inside a city.

Working farmland is valued by what the ground earns rather than by what a developer might pay, a rule found in Section 172A of the state constitution. Ask the PVA to show how each of your acres is classified before you price a farm.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Madison County households and housing?
sections.html:
Census Bureau estimates for 2020 to 2024 describe a county centered on its two campuses, with a median owner-occupied home value of $232,000.

The county gained 9.7 percent in population between the 2020 base and mid-2025. Employer establishments numbered 1,808 in 2023, with total payroll near $1.19 billion, and 2022 retail sales reached $1.76 billion.

The median age at the 2020 census was 35.6, and the county's decade-by-decade jumps tell the same story: up 27.6 percent in the 1970 count and 24.9 percent in 1980. Today 16.1 percent of residents are 65 or older, 20.4 percent are under 18, and 5,522 are veterans. Households average 2.43 people, 84.2 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier, and per capita income is $32,828. Roughly 16.4 percent of residents live below the poverty line, a figure that includes many students.

sections.h2: How late can a Madison County bill be paid before it costs more?
sections.html:
The sheriff's tax page does not publish a dated calendar and tells owners to follow the periods printed on the bill or in the online portal. The standard timetable behind those periods is in KRS 134.015.

  • A full payment made by the first of November takes two percent off.
  • The following two months, through December, call for the face amount.
  • During January a five percent charge appears.
  • From February onward the charge is ten percent of the unpaid tax.

When bills are delayed, the Department of Revenue can substitute a shorter schedule that starts from the mailing date. Collection fees are layered on top for delinquent bills, and the Department of Revenue's guide says interest of one percent a month runs once the bill reaches the clerk.

The Madison County Clerk's home page carries a 2025 delinquent county property tax list in two parts, marked as updated August 31, 2026, plus a page for third-party purchasers. Pull your own parcel up there before you list. The County Attorney's office also runs delinquent collection and says an installment agreement signed before the Clerk's sale keeps a bill from being bought by an investor. Its number is 624-4777, extension 9.

sections.h2: Can I contest my Madison County assessment?
sections.html:
Yes. Ask the PVA for a conference first, then file a written petition with the County Clerk if the answer is unsatisfactory. KRS 133.120, amended effective July 15, 2026, sets the timing, and a hearing before the county board follows. Attach sales of similar properties, insurance records or an appraisal. Paying on your claimed value continues during the appeal.

For a house near a campus, good comparables come from recent sales of similar homes close to yours. For acreage, ask the PVA which agricultural class applies. The board's calendar is fixed by KRS 133.030, which puts the first meeting 25 to 35 days after inspection closes.

sections.h2: Who qualifies for the Madison County homestead exemption?
sections.html: Owners aged 65 or over, and owners classified as totally disabled, who live in the home. The statewide amount is $49,100 for 2025 and 2026, so a house valued at $232,000 is taxed as if it were worth $182,900. The Madison County PVA takes applications, and the sheriff points owners with exemption questions to that office. When the home sells, the buyer has to apply for any exemption of their own.

sections.h2: What do I need to clear before a Madison County closing?
sections.html:
Request a payoff from the sheriff for the current bill and check the clerk's delinquent list for older years. The sheriff's guidance says taxes are commonly prorated at closing and that the current owner is the one who must make sure the bill is paid, so read the settlement statement line by line.

A lien from delinquent tax follows the land for up to eleven years under KRS 134.015(5), so a title company will ask for it to be cleared whoever holds title.

Deeds are recorded at the Richmond Branch of the Clerk, (859) 624-4703, extension 3. The Clerk's records reach back to 1786 and are searched by a person's name only. Documents from 1986 forward are scanned and available in person or through the subscription service ECCLIX. E-recordings are processed daily until about 9:30 to 10:00 in the morning. The office also offers DocAlert, a free service that sends a notice if anything is recorded under your name or against your property. Kentucky's transfer tax of $0.50 per $500 of value under KRS 142.050 would be $232 on a sale at the Census median value.

faqs.q: Does the Madison County Sheriff take online payments?
faqs.a: Yes. The sheriff's tax page links to a secure portal for searching and paying bills, and the portal shows any service fee before you submit. In-person and mail payments are also accepted.

faqs.q: What is the Madison County homestead exemption for 2026?
faqs.a: $49,100, the same figure that applies to the 2025 assessment year. Apply with the PVA if you are 65 or older or totally disabled.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed in Madison County?
faqs.a: At the County Clerk's Richmond Branch, 321 N. Madison Ave. The recordings desk is at (859) 624-4703, extension 3.

faqs.q: Who can help if my Madison County tax bill is delinquent?
faqs.a: The County Attorney's delinquent tax office, reachable at 624-4777 extension 9. It may offer an installment agreement if you act before the Clerk's sale.

faqs.q: Do Madison County tax bills go to the buyer after a sale?
faqs.a: Not automatically. The sheriff says taxes are commonly prorated at closing and the current owner must see that the bill is paid, so confirm who is paying with the closing agent.
